data.name: Chainless
data.detailed_description:
Escape from prison and swing your way through the city, avoid various obstacles, don't get caught and try not to fall.
Compete with friends and rise to the top of the leaderboard!

VR Fitness Insider review: 4/5

Features:
  • Realistic swinging-physics
  • Global leaderboard & personal statistics
  • Achievements
  • Frequent updates
  • Randomly generated environment every new run!
  • Comfort settings ("anti-motion sickness")

Bonus:
  • Humor & easter eggs
  • Feel (and look) like Tarzan
  • Sore arms

Planned features:
  • Multiplayer mode! - in the works
  • Cosmetic appearance
  • Multiple environments

Escape, swing, fall, repeat.


"But, why is the game called Chainless when there is so many chains?"
Ssshhh

"Why are the chains floating?"
... sshhhhh less questions more swinging.

I designed this game because I personally felt like VR lacked content that could be played for more than just a few hours - that was my goal, which I hope I have achieved in your opinion - if not, feedback is appreciated in the Discussion section!
Happy swinging!

reviews.review:
Chainless is a compact virtual reality action experience that builds almost everything around movement, momentum, and the unusual pleasure of swinging through an environment using chains. Developed and published by Albert MN, the game embraces the experimental spirit of early room-scale VR and turns a very simple concept into an arcade-style challenge. Instead of overwhelming the player with complicated systems or a lengthy narrative, it concentrates on escaping, staying alive, maintaining momentum, and traveling as far as possible without making a costly mistake.

The defining mechanic involves grabbing chains and using them to swing through the environment. It sounds straightforward, but successfully linking one swing into another requires surprisingly careful timing. Players need to judge distance, understand momentum, release at the correct moment, and quickly locate another chain before gravity brings the run to an abrupt conclusion. Early attempts can feel awkward as the physics take some getting used to, but improvement is noticeable. Eventually, movements that initially require conscious thought begin to feel much more natural, producing an enjoyable rhythm of grabbing, swinging, releasing, and recovering.

There is a satisfying physical quality to the experience because the VR motion controls make the player's arms an important part of navigation. Rather than pressing a button to perform an elaborate traversal maneuver, players physically reach toward their next connection. This makes successful movement feel more personal and immediate. It can also become tiring during extended sessions, particularly when aggressively reaching and swinging repeatedly. Chainless therefore works best in relatively short sessions where its energetic movement remains entertaining rather than exhausting.

The objective is presented through a lighthearted prison-escape scenario. Players must keep moving through the city while avoiding obstacles, dangerous falls, and the threat of being caught. The premise is not intended to deliver a complicated story. Instead, it provides a playful excuse for the endless movement. The game is quite self-aware about the strange sight of chains floating around the environment and generally treats its own concept with humor rather than attempting to explain everything seriously.

Randomly generated environments are especially important to its replay value. Because the fundamental interaction does not dramatically change, procedural layouts help prevent every attempt from becoming an exercise in memorization. Players have to react to new situations and make rapid decisions about where to swing next. Random generation cannot completely hide the limited scope of the mechanics, but it gives repeated runs a stronger sense of unpredictability and makes mechanical skill more valuable than simply remembering an ideal route.

The arcade structure is reinforced by personal statistics and global leaderboard functionality. Instead of finishing the experience once and having little reason to return, players can concentrate on improving previous performances and comparing results. Steam achievements add another layer of objectives for completion-oriented players. These supporting systems fit the design particularly well because Chainless is fundamentally about repeated attempts and gradual mastery rather than progressing through an elaborate campaign.

Comfort is an important consideration because swinging, falling, acceleration, and artificial movement in VR can be demanding. The game includes options intended to reduce motion sickness, which is a sensible addition for this style of locomotion. Even so, comfort will vary substantially between individuals. Experienced VR players accustomed to artificial movement are likely to adapt more easily, while newcomers or people particularly susceptible to VR sickness may need shorter sessions.

Visually and structurally, Chainless is modest. The presentation primarily exists to support the movement system rather than showcase highly detailed environments or cinematic storytelling. This simplicity has advantages because the player's attention remains focused on locating chains and planning the next movement. However, it also exposes the game's biggest weakness: there simply is not an enormous amount of mechanical variety. Players looking for deep combat, character development, extensive exploration, or a lengthy narrative adventure are unlikely to find those elements here.

The experience is better suited to players who appreciate experimental VR mechanics and score-driven challenges. Its satisfaction comes from becoming more comfortable with the physics and gradually transforming clumsy early attempts into smooth sequences of connected swings. The leaderboard, achievements, statistics, procedural layouts, humor, and physical controls provide enough surrounding structure to support that central mechanic, although they cannot completely overcome the repetition that eventually develops.

Steam Deck compatibility is effectively unsupported for normal Steam Deck play because Chainless is designed as a VR-only experience requiring compatible virtual reality hardware and tracked motion controls. It should therefore not be considered a practical native handheld game for the Steam Deck's built-in display and controls. Even if technical workarounds are possible through a broader PC VR setup, that is fundamentally different from conventional Deck gameplay.

Overall, Chainless succeeds most when treated as a focused VR arcade experiment rather than a full-sized adventure. Its chain-swinging physics provide an unusual form of locomotion that becomes more rewarding as the player learns how to control momentum, while procedural generation and competitive features encourage repeated attempts. Limited variety and reliance on VR hardware restrict its audience, but its energetic movement and playful personality give it a distinct identity.

Rating: 7/10
